rootCauseOneLine: status-changed realtime pushes carry no row data and the app's registry rule for them invalidates the single monolithic sidebarNavigation query (full ThreadListEntry for every visible thread of every project, ~1 KB/row) with an immediate flush, so every turn start/end re-downloads the whole 134 KB bootstrap instead of patching one row.
proposedFix: (1) Add optional status/runtime to threadChangeMetadataSchema, have every notifyThread(["status-changed"]) caller include the post-transition values, and change the app's status-changed rule to patch the row in the thread-list and sidebar caches (mirroring the existing hasPendingInteraction patch path), falling back to the current dirtyThreadListQueries only when metadata is missing or the row is not cached; server<->app only, no daemon protocol bump. (2) Introduce a trimmed sidebarThreadEntrySchema for sidebar-bootstrap threads and drop per-project sources/defaultExecutionOptions from the bootstrap. (3) Optionally scope remaining refetches per project (per-project query keys or ?projectId= on the route) and give status-changed the 50 ms debounce once it is a cache patch.
caveats: Measured on the Vite dev build (React dev runtime), so absolute CPU numbers are inflated; ratios and byte counts are what matter. JSON parse and whole-tree re-render claims in the issue are overstated (parse ~1 ms at 6x throttle; structural sharing keeps unchanged rows), the real per-event cost is wire bytes + one server-side full list read + O(all threads) deep-compare. The 650-930 ms render on idle->active is the active-row reorder and would occur with a patch too. Side finding: pnpm seed:perf fails with a FOREIGN KEY error if the dev server is running (destroyed-environment prune races the seed); it must be run with the server stopped. Worktree HEAD was a108fa7ef on start; I checked out 16ceb3a54 for all measurements.
